title: Wander navigation messages
description: Payloads exchanged between the iPhone (Niantic Lightship SDK / ARKit), the FastAPI backend on Modal, and the web dashboard. All positions are metres in the world's frame (the frame `alignment` maps the splat into — normally the Niantic VPS site frame). Rotations are unit quaternions [x, y, z, w].

localizationUpdate.title: LocalizationUpdate
localizationUpdate.description: Sent by the phone every time the Niantic SDK returns a VPS localization result (or ARKit drifts enough to re-report).

sessionId.description: Omit on the first call; the backend returns one.

deviceId.description: Stable per-install id; also identifies the role (chest / left / back) via `role`.

nianticSiteId.description: Lightship VPS location the phone localised against. Must match the world's manifest.

pose.description: Camera pose in the VPS site frame as reported by the SDK (`ARLocalizationResult` / `LocalizationTarget` transform).
Pose re-expressed in the world frame (identical to the input when alignment.frame is the VPS frame).

snappedPosition.description: Position projected onto the closest graph edge.

oneOf.description: Free position; snapped to the nearest edge.

from.description: Defaults to the session's last known position when omitted.

to.description: Destination node id (usually kind = destination), or `note:<noteId>` for a note pinned in the web viewer: the route then ends at the point on the nearest walkable edge beside the note, as a virtual node named after it.

avoid.description: Node ids to route around (e.g. closed doors).

headingDeg.description: Traveller's heading at `from` (world convention: clockwise from above, 0 = -Z, 90 = +X). The first instruction turns relative to it; without it the first turn is 'straight'.

accessibleOnly.description: Skip edges whose `accessible` is false (stairs, escalators, stepped paths); floor changes then go by elevator or ramp.

headingDeg.description: Compass-style heading in the world frame, 0 = -Z, clockwise.

turn.description: Turn bucket, or the vertical transition to take (stairs / escalator / elevator / ramp) when the next leg changes floors.

text.description: Short spoken cue, e.g. 'Left at Reception desk, then continue 12 metres, passing Bottle filler on your right.' or 'Take the elevator to floor 2'.

landmarks.description: Human-reviewed annotations woven into `text`: `at` sits within 3 m of the turn node; `left`/`right` is passed beside the leg. Positions come from the published graph/notes, never from the language model.

destination.description: Destination node id, or `note:<noteId>` for a pinned note (see routeRequest.to). Absent when no guidance is active; DELETE /sessions/{id}/destination clears it.

accessibleOnly.description: Every route and reroute in this session is computed with `accessibleOnly`.

poseUpdate.title: PoseUpdate
poseUpdate.description: High-rate pose from ARKit between VPS fixes (5–10 Hz is plenty).

offRouteMetres.description: Perpendicular distance from the route; > 3 m flips state to off-route.

speak.description: Exact phrase the phone should say now, if any.

headingDeg.description: Traveller's heading derived from the pose rotation (0 = -Z, 90 = +X, clockwise). `instruction` is relative to it.

sessionEvent.title: SessionEvent
sessionEvent.description: Envelope pushed over the WebSocket to the web dashboard (and optionally back to the phone).

localizationQueryRequest.title: LocalizationQueryRequest
localizationQueryRequest.description: The Niantic SDK's own record of one VPS network request (`Vps2LocalizationRequestRecord`), mirrored so the dashboard can show what happened to the frame.

frameId.description: `NSDKFrameData.frameId` of the camera frame that was submitted.

error.description: `Vps2LocalizationError` case name; "none" when the request succeeded.

frameMatch.description: How the phone paired the request with a camera frame: by frameId, by timestamp, or the newest frame it still held.

localizationQueryResult.title: LocalizationQueryResult
localizationQueryResult.description: What the query produced. `pose` is the camera pose at the moment the query frame was captured, in the VPS site frame (anchor⁻¹ · camera), so it can be drawn on the splat.

currentPose.description: Where the phone is now (site frame), if it has moved since the frame was captured.

path.description: Volume path of the stored JPEG, e.g. worlds/<id>/localizations/<queryId>.jpg (set by the backend).

orientation.description: portrait: image up = camera −X, image right = camera +Y (ARKit landscape-right sensor rotated 90° CW). landscape: image axes = camera axes.

fovDeg.description: Field of view of the uploaded image (after any rotation / downscale), for drawing the frustum.

localizationQueryUpload.title: LocalizationQueryUpload
localizationQueryUpload.description: Sent by the phone for every VPS image query the Niantic SDK issued: the camera frame it submitted (JPEG), the SDK's request record, and the resulting pose. `POST /worlds/{id}/localize/query`.

capturedAt.description: Wall-clock time the camera frame was captured.

localizationQuery.title: LocalizationQuery
localizationQuery.description: Stored record of one image query (`worlds/<id>/localizations/index.json`, newest first). Same as the upload without the image bytes, plus ids, the stored image path, and the nearest graph node.

vpsSiteStatus.title: VpsSiteStatus
vpsSiteStatus.description: What the backend knows about the Niantic Lightship VPS location behind a world.

localizable.description: Lightship reports the location as activated / localizable.

meshAvailable.description: A VPS mesh export exists on the volume (assets.vpsMap).

lastLocalizedAt.description: Most recent successful phone localization against this site.
